messages:
Maria: Quick update — ran multi-GPU perf sweep this morning focusing on NCCL tuning for our TP=2 / 8xA100 nodes. Goal: understand all-reduce start gaps and whether CHUNKS/CHANNELS/PROTO settings improve comm/compute overlap.
Joe: Good. Synthetic or live workload?
Maria: Both. Started with nccl-tests microbench to map baseline latency/throughput, then replayed an inference trace with dynamic batching + KV cache warm/cold scenarios.
Sam: Anything changed in driver stack recently? last month we saw a cudnn regression.
Maria: Stack is stable: driver 525.105, CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.2.2. I reproduced a ~9% p95 tail regression on seq=1024 compared to our older baseline.
Kevin: 9% tail is notable. Do we know if it's compute or comm-triggered?
Maria: Profiled with Nsight Systems. Timeline shows compute finishes, then a gap before ncclAllReduce posts — gaps around ~200us on some ranks. Increasing NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE shrank that gap.
perf-bot: [auto] Uploaded nccl-tests sweep artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/nccl/1719621123/
Joe: What parameter matrix did you run?
Maria: Matrix included NCCL_NTHREADS(default), CHANNELS=1,2,4,8; NCCL_PROTO=LL,LL128,SIMPLE; ALGO=RING,TREE; and chunk sizes 1MB/4MB/8MB. Also ran LL128 on/off.
Observations:
- CHANNELS=1: quieter for tiny messages but lower aggregate throughput for our 256B-16KB tokens.
- CHANNELS=4: best steady throughput across our real token mix.
- Enabling LL128 with CHANNELS=4 + RING reduced p95/p99 most consistently.
- On our 40GbE cluster, NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE ~8MB minimized the compute->comm gap.
Sam: Did you try different NIC/RDMA toggles?
Maria: RN: toggled NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX and tested RDMA vs. IPoIB; this cluster fell back to Ethernet path so no clear RDMA gains. On RDMA clusters we expect LL128 larger wins.
Kevin: How does KV cache behavior change this? fewer kv updates should mean fewer collectives?
Maria: Exactly. Warm-cache runs show ~18% fewer all-reduces, which lowers contention and smooths p95. Cold-cache bursts still cause the worst tail spikes where overlap matters.
Joe: Any interaction with kernel selection? e.g., long-seq matmul variant?
Maria: Yes — when the runtime picks the long-sequence GEMM kernel (seq>=1024), compute time grows but becomes more uniform, which helped hide comm: larger compute slabs give NCCL more time to schedule ops and reduced effective gaps. However mixed batches (short+long kernels) fragment compute and hurt overlap.
Sam: So cohorting by sequence length might help?
Maria: Exactly. Proposed quick wins I prototyped:
- Default CHANNELS=4 on 8-GPU nodes for our token distribution.
- Prefer PROTO=LL128 with RING on RDMA-capable clusters; fallback to LL on legacy NICs.
- Tune NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE to ~8MB for our 40GbE profile.
- Implement cohort batching flag so the scheduler groups requests by seq-length bucket before kernel selection.
Kevin: Who owns the runtime change for cohort batching?
Maria: I'll prototype a feature-flagged change tomorrow, plus a canary rollout plan.
Joe: Can we add an automated perf job that simulates cold-KV bursts so regressions are alerted?
Maria: Yep — adding a Jenkins perf job that runs cold/warm traces against the NCCL matrix and uploads Nsight timelines to S3.
perf-bot: [note] Created PERF-3187 to track follow-ups.
Sam: Be careful with enabling LL128 broadly; older NICs can regress. Need a capability probe at agent startup.
Maria: Plan is to detect NIC capabilities on agent init and set NCCL envs, with an override toggle in Console for ops.
Kevin: Once patched and validated, canary to 10% of Dedicated infra.
Maria: Will do. Attaching a trimmed Nsight timeline snippet (times are relative ms):
``n[rank0] compute_done       12.342ms
[rank0] gap_start         12.342ms
[rank0] nccl_allreduce_st 12.544ms  <-- 202us gap
[rank1] compute_done       12.350ms
[rank1] nccl_allreduce_st 12.548ms
```nAfter CHANNELS=4 + PROTO=LL128 + chunk=8MB:
``n[rank0] compute_done       12.342ms
[rank0] nccl_allreduce_st 12.360ms  <-- 18us gap
```nThis reduced p99 and tail jitter significantly in the testbed.
Joe: Solid. Please attach S3 links to the Nsight captures once Jenkins finishes.
Maria: Will do. TL;DR: CHANNELS=4 + LL128 + chunk tuning + cohort batching prototype => p99 down ~12%, tail ~20% on our traces.
